subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Testing (types of test and test data)

questions.q: What is the main aim of defensive design when writing programs?
options: To anticipate how a program could be misused and prevent problems before they occur
To make the program run as fast as possible
To reduce the number of lines of code used
To make the user interface more colourful
questions.explain: Defensive design anticipates misuse and unexpected inputs so the program stays robust.

questions.q: Which validation check ensures that a number entered lies between a set minimum and maximum?
options: Range check
Presence check
Type check
Format check
questions.explain: A range check confirms a value falls within defined lower and upper limits.

questions.q: A presence check is used to make sure that...
options: a required field has not been left empty
data is of the correct data type
data matches a set pattern
a value is within an allowed range
questions.explain: A presence check verifies that data has actually been entered into a required field.

questions.q: Requiring a user to log in with a username and password before using a system is an example of...
options: Authentication
Indentation
Iteration
Interpretation
questions.explain: Authentication confirms a user's identity, a key defensive design technique.

questions.q: Which two types of testing are identified in the OCR specification?
options: Iterative testing and terminal (final) testing
Alpha testing and beta testing
Black-box and white-box testing
Unit testing and stress testing
questions.explain: OCR identifies iterative testing during development and terminal testing of the finished program.

questions.q: Iterative testing is best described as...
options: testing modules repeatedly during development and fixing errors as you go
testing only once the whole program is finished
testing carried out by the end customer
testing that measures the program's speed under load
questions.explain: Iterative testing happens throughout development, checking each part as it is built.

questions.q: Normal test data is best described as...
options: sensible, valid data that the program is expected to accept
data at the extreme edges of the accepted range
data of the wrong type that should be rejected
data deliberately designed to crash the program
questions.explain: Normal data is typical valid input that the program should process without issue.

questions.q: How do comments in source code help maintainability?
options: They explain what parts of the code do, helping other programmers understand it
They make the program execute more quickly
They automatically fix syntax errors
They encrypt the code so it cannot be copied
questions.explain: Comments document the code, making it easier for others to read and update later.

questions.q: Why does thorough input validation make a program more robust?
options: It prevents invalid or unexpected data from causing crashes or incorrect results
It increases the program's execution speed
It reduces the amount of memory the program uses
It removes the need for any testing
questions.explain: Validation stops unsuitable data being processed, helping the program cope with misuse.

questions.q: A form must accept postcodes in the pattern 'LL9 9LL' (letters and digits in a fixed order). Which validation check is most appropriate?
options: Format check
Range check
Presence check
Length check
questions.explain: A format check confirms that data matches a required pattern of characters.

questions.q: A field should only accept whole numbers. Which validation check best enforces this?
options: Type check
Presence check
Format check
Range check
questions.explain: A type check confirms that the entered data is of the expected data type.

questions.q: How does terminal (final) testing differ from iterative testing?
options: It is carried out on the completed program as a whole, rather than during development
It is carried out before any code is written
It only checks the spelling of on-screen messages
It is performed automatically by the compiler
questions.explain: Terminal testing checks the finished program against the requirements once it is complete.

questions.q: What best distinguishes erroneous data from invalid data?
options: Erroneous data is of the wrong type, whereas invalid data is the right type but outside the accepted range
Erroneous data is always numeric, whereas invalid data is always text
They are two names for exactly the same thing
Invalid data is data the program accepts, while erroneous data is data it rejects
questions.explain: Both should be rejected, but erroneous data is the wrong type while invalid data is the correct type out of range.

questions.q: Why does consistent indentation improve maintainability?
options: It visually shows the structure and nesting of code blocks, making it easier to read
It makes the program run using less memory
It is required or no program will ever compile
It automatically adds comments to the code
questions.explain: Indentation reveals how blocks such as loops and conditions are nested, aiding readability.

questions.q: Why are descriptive variable names such as 'totalScore' preferred over names like 'x'?
options: They make the purpose of each variable clear, improving readability and maintainability
They make the program run faster
They use less storage space
They prevent the variable from being changed
questions.explain: Meaningful names show what each variable stores, making code easier to follow and update.

questions.q: How does dividing a program into subprograms (functions and procedures) aid maintainability?
options: It creates reusable, self-contained blocks that are easier to understand, test and update
It guarantees the program contains no logic errors
It removes the need for any variables
It makes the program impossible to edit
questions.explain: Subprograms break a task into modular, reusable units that simplify reading and maintenance.

questions.q: A program must only accept exam marks from 0 to 100 inclusive. Which validation rule enforces this?
options: A range check that accepts values from 0 to 100 inclusive
A presence check that the field is not blank
A length check limiting entry to three characters
A type check that the value is text
questions.explain: A range check restricts entries to the allowed lower and upper limits of the mark scale.

questions.q: A registration form must ensure a mobile number contains exactly 11 characters. Which check should be used?
options: Length check
Range check
Type check
Presence check
questions.explain: A length check confirms the data has the required number of characters.

questions.q: A temperature field accepts whole numbers from 0 to 40. A tester enters 100. What category of test data is this?
options: Invalid data
Normal data
Boundary data
Erroneous data
questions.explain: 100 is the correct type but outside the accepted range, so it is invalid data.

questions.q: A field accepts whole numbers from 1 to 10. Which entry is an example of erroneous data?
options: 'ten' typed as text
questions.explain: Erroneous data is the wrong type; 5 is normal, 10 is boundary and 11 would be invalid.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Computer Science (J277) specification; Producing Robust Programs
